title: Rockies bench Cole Carrigg for giving middle finger to Braves fans, then use him as pinch hitter
content:
ATLANTA – Colorado Rockies manager Warren Schaeffer said before Sunday’s game that rookie outfielder Cole Carrigg would be sitting out “a couple days” after he was caught on Saturday’s broadcast giving a middle finger to Atlanta Braves fans during Colorado’s 2-1 loss at Truist Park.

Carrigg’s punishment lasted only six innings.

The incident happened in the eighth inning after Carrigg dove for a ball hit by Michael Harris II and missed by a few inches. The hit scored two runs, and the Braves took the lead. Shortly after getting up, Carrigg extended his middle finger.

“First, I apologize to my teammates and the organization, that’s not how I want to represent us,” Carrigg told MLB.com before Sunday’s series finale. “That’s inexcusable on my part. With that being said, I’m somebody who’s going to play at 110 percent every game and give my all to this team and to the game to try to win ballgames. That was a play that I felt could or could not have won the game, so I’m very passionate about that.”

On Sunday, with the Rockies down 2-1 in the seventh inning, Mickey Moniak’s two-out single led to the Braves replacing starter Tyler Mahle with Dylan Dodd. Schaefer countered by using Carrigg to pinch hit for Troy Johnson. Carrigg struck out swinging and remained in the game as the Rockies’ center fielder.

The Rockies went into Sunday with a 52-84 record and were trying to avoid being swept by the Braves. Carrigg, however, has been one of the influx of homegrown players who have contributed in recent weeks.

The 24-year-old is hitting .263/.345/.444 with six home runs, and his .789 OPS ranks fifth among qualified rookies. His nine doubles in August are the fifth-most in the majors, making him one of 12 rookies in Rockies history to accomplish that feat. His 28.7 mph sprint speed ranks in the 86th percentile and has helped him steal eight bases and cover plenty of ground in the outfield.

Carrigg was known for his temper in the minors and has been ejected in the past.

“Cole made a mistake. He knows that is an embarrassment to the organization and that we don’t stand for that,” said Schaeffer. “Listen, everybody makes mistakes. It’s just one that he has to learn from. It’s just that we will not put up with that here.”
